references.text: Elijah calls Elisha to follow him, and Elisha leaves everything—the oxen and his family—to follow the prophet. This is a parallel to how Levi left everything and followed Jesus.
Simon, Andrew, James, and John left their nets and boat and immediately followed Jesus, just as Levi left everything and followed him.
Matthew's parallel account of the calling of the tax collector Levi (Matthew), where Jesus says, 'Follow me,' and he got up and followed him.
Peter says to Jesus, 'We have left everything and followed you.' This reflects the radical choice Levi made when he left everything to follow Jesus.
Mark's parallel account of the calling of Levi, son of Alphaeus, who was sitting at the tax booth, stood up, and followed Jesus.
Peter says: 'We have left everything and followed you.' The same theme of leaving all to follow Jesus, as Levi did.
Just before in Luke's account, Simon Peter, James, and John leave their boats and everything they had to follow Jesus—the same pattern as Levi's calling.
Jesus says that whoever does not give up all that he owns cannot be his disciple. Levi is a concrete example of this principle.
Peter says: 'We have left everything we owned and followed you.' This theme of leaving all is directly linked to Levi's action.
Paul counted everything he had as loss in order to gain Christ. The same radical prioritization that Levi showed when he left everything at the tax booth to follow Jesus.
